Welcome to St Lawrence College
St Lawrence College has a rich history and a reputation for excellence. The genuine feeling of community is tangible and there is no doubt that the Christian values, boarding ethos, all-through nature of the school and focus on the individual contribute to a feeling of care and compassion that permeates every corner of the campus. It is my honour and privilege to be leading such an outstanding school.

Today is Ash Wednesday, marking the beginning of Lent—a season of prayer, fasting, and charitable giving in preparation for Easter. Rooted in the 40 days that Jesus spent fasting in the wilderness, Lent encourages Christians to practise self-discipline, seek spiritual renewal, and extend generosity to those in need.During this time, many in our school community are also observing Ramadan, a sacred month of fasting, prayer, and acts of kindness leading up to Eid. A time of deep spiritual reflection and devotion, Ramadan commemorates the revelation of the Qur’an to the Prophet Muhammad and encourages self-restraint and generosity.Though distinct in practice, both seasons call for reflection, discipline, and compassion—values that unite us across faiths and beliefs. As a school built on a strong Christian ethos, we are committed to fostering an environment where all students, of all faiths and none, feel supported in their spiritual journeys.Our latest news story explores these shared values and their place in our community. Read more on our website.#StLawrenceCollege #ChristianEthos #Lent #Ramadan #FaithAndReflection #AllFaithsAndNone #SchoolCommunity ...

Creative Arts at St Lawrence College
Creative Arts are a vibrant part of life at St Lawrence College, offering every student the opportunity to express themselves, think independently, and develop technical and conceptual skills across a range of disciplines. Our provision in Art, Photography, Drama (including LAMDA), and Design Technology enables pupils to explore their creativity in depth, guided by expert staff in purpose-built facilities.
From Year 7 through to Sixth Form, students are supported to build confidence, embrace experimentation, and produce work they are proud of — whether on canvas, stage, screen or in the workshop.
Music
Music is a central part of life at St Lawrence College. Our aim is to nurture an appreciation and understanding of music across a wide range of genres and styles, while encouraging pupils to experience the joy of performing. From concerts and ensembles to recording and composing, students are given every opportunity to develop both their skills and their love for music.
Academic Music
All pupils receive classroom music lessons in Years 7 and 8, exploring musical elements, listening skills, composition, and performance. From Year 9 onwards, music becomes an optional subject at GCSE and A Level. Our curriculum is designed to challenge and inspire musicians of all abilities.
The Music Department is well-equipped, featuring a main classroom with a suite of iMacs, a professional recording studio, and a range of practice rooms to support solo and group rehearsal.
Please see our academics page for more details.
Performance Opportunities
We offer a wide variety of ensembles and performance groups, including:
Popular highlights of the year include our House Singing Competition and the high-energy Battle of the Bands. Regular concerts give all musicians—from beginners to advanced performers—the chance to take the stage and share their talents.
Orchestra
Senior and Kirby Choirs
Jazz Band
Rock Band
Student-led ensembles tailored to pupil strengths
Individual Tuition
Many pupils take individual instrumental or vocal lessons with our team of expert visiting music teachers. Tuition is available across a wide range of instruments and musical styles. Pupils consistently achieve Distinctions and Merits in ABRSM, Trinity, and Rockschool graded examinations.
Click here to view our Music Lesson Information Pack and Booking Form.
Beyond the Classroom
Musical enrichment at SLC extends beyond campus. Pupils enjoy regular trips to concerts in London and the local area, as well as in-house workshops and masterclasses led by visiting professional musicians.
Music tours are a much-loved part of our co-curricular programme. Recent highlights include the Kirby Choir’s performance at Disneyland Paris and in one of the city’s historic churches.
Scholarships
Music Scholarships are offered at 11+, 13+, and 16+ to talented pupils who demonstrate musical ability and potential. For more information or to apply, please contact our Registrar at admissions@slcuk.com.
Facilities
Art
At St Lawrence College, Art is a vibrant and essential part of school life — a subject where students are encouraged to be bold, curious, and expressive. Through a carefully designed and progressive curriculum, pupils develop their own artistic voice while mastering a range of traditional and contemporary techniques.
From Foundation to Mastery
In Key Stage 3, students begin their artistic journey by building core skills in drawing, observation, and idea development. These are explored through creative projects that foster experimentation, confidence, and personal reflection.
At GCSE level (AQA Art & Design), pupils work on sustained and personalised projects, refining their techniques across painting, printmaking, sculpture, and mixed media. A-Level students can specialise in Art, Craft & Design, immersing themselves in an independent creative process that encourages innovation, personal inquiry, and mastery of materials.
Please see our academics page for more details.
Artistic Development & Individual Support
Open-ended tasks, expert one-to-one guidance, and small group critiques allow each student to flourish creatively at their own pace. We nurture not only technical skill, but also critical thinking, visual literacy, and expressive communication.
Beyond the Classroom
Pupils participate in a wide range of enrichment opportunities, including life drawing sessions, artist-led workshops, gallery trips (such as the Turner Contemporary and exhibitions in London), and entries into prestigious competitions like the Royal Academy’s Young Artists Summer Show. Their work is regularly showcased in the department’s own gallery, celebrating creativity across all year groups.
A Creative Future
The skills gained through art — from problem-solving to creative risk-taking — are highly transferable and form the foundation for careers in fine art, design, branding, illustration, architecture, and more.
Meet Levi
Facilities
Photography
Photography at St Lawrence College is where visual storytelling meets cutting-edge creativity. Offered as a dedicated A-Level pathway, it empowers students to see the world through a new lens; both literally and conceptually.
Independent and Experimental
Our students explore the art of photography through technical skill-building, critical analysis, and hands-on experimentation. They engage with both analogue and digital formats, developing proficiency in studio lighting, composition, darkroom processing, image manipulation and Adobe editing software.
Curriculum Depth
Following the AQA Photography specification, students produce highly individualised portfolios and coursework. Emphasis is placed on independent exploration of themes and building a strong personal aesthetic. The subject encourages reflection, resilience, and creative risk-taking, all supported by specialist guidance in a well-resourced, dedicated studio.
Please see our academics page for more details.
Real-World Inspiration
To deepen engagement with the wider photographic world, students take part in gallery visits and creative workshops. Trips to London and New York provide opportunities to study the work of established photographers and artists, while enriching their cultural and visual understanding.
Pathways & Preparation
With growing demand for visual communication across industries, Photography opens doors to careers in media, advertising, branding, content creation, editorial, and digital design. Students receive tailored support for university applications, portfolio development, and progression into creative industries.
Meet Ileri
Facilities
Drama
Drama at St Lawrence College is an energetic and inclusive space where creativity, collaboration and confidence take centre stage. Students are encouraged to explore performance in all its forms – from acting and directing to design and production – within a vibrant and supportive theatrical environment.
Performance with Purpose
Our curriculum goes far beyond the script. Through devising, rehearsing and analysing live theatre, students learn to express complex ideas, connect with diverse perspectives, and reflect on the world around them. Regular performance opportunities, including two major productions a year, House Drama, and Theatre Thursday showcases allow students to refine their craft and celebrate their progress in front of an audience.
A Home for Creativity
Drama is taught in Taylor Hall, our 500-seat professional-standard theatre, complete with modern lighting and sound systems, costume storage and dressing rooms. Whether it’s Shakespeare, musicals or contemporary devised theatre, students bring stories to life in a space built to inspire. All pupils study Drama as part of the curriculum up to Year 8, with options to continue at GCSE and A-Level for those seeking to deepen their skills.
Please see our academics page for more details.
LAMDA: Confidence that Lasts a Lifetime
Speech and Drama lessons (LAMDA) are a cornerstone of our co-curricular offering. Taught individually or in small groups, LAMDA empowers students to develop powerful communication skills, build stage presence and prepare for nationally recognised qualifications — including those that carry UCAS points at Grades 6–8. Pupils can specialise in Acting, Public Speaking, Mime, Verse and Prose, Shakespeare and more.
Culture, Competition, and Celebration
Trips to professional theatre productions, visiting companies and workshops with industry experts bring the wider world of theatre into the classroom. Events like Arts Fortnight and Drama Scholarships add richness and momentum to the calendar, while performance pathways ensure every student can find their role — whether on stage or behind the scenes.
Creative Futures
Drama nurtures adaptable, articulate and resilient individuals. Students graduate with transferable skills in communication, problem-solving and teamwork — qualities that are essential in careers from law and teaching to business, broadcasting, media and the performing arts. For those who love the energy of theatre and the power of expression, Drama at SLC is the perfect stage.
Facilities
Design Technology
Design Technology at St Lawrence College blends innovation, functionality and imagination — equipping students to think, prototype and problem-solve like true creatives in an ever-evolving world.
Innovation in Action
More than just making, DT at SLC is about meaningful creation. Students explore the full lifecycle of design: from concept and planning to execution and evaluation. They work across a wide range of materials and technologies, gaining hands-on experience with 3D printing, laser cutting, electronics, and textiles. From product design to wearable tech, every brief encourages purpose-driven innovation.
Personal Projects, Real Outcomes
With a curriculum that evolves from Key Stage 3 through to A-Level, students take on increasingly ambitious and personalised design challenges. At GCSE and A-Level, projects are student-led, allowing for exploration in areas like sustainability, inclusive design, smart materials, and engineered systems. Whether designing for user needs or tackling environmental issues, our students are empowered to think critically and creatively.
Please see our academics page for more details.
A Studio for Discovery
Our well-equipped workshops are dynamic spaces where creativity meets precision. Students use professional-standard CAD software and fabrication tools to realise their ideas, guided by expert tuition and individual feedback. This environment fosters independent thinking and problem-solving skills — essential not just for exams, but for future pathways.
Design Thinking Beyond the Classroom
DT students regularly engage in national competitions like Design Ventura and experience workshops led by real-world designers and engineers. The department also offers exciting enrichment such as Robot Wars, DT Ambassadors, and trips to the Design Museum and V&A — extending learning beyond textbooks and into authentic, inspiring contexts.
Future-Ready Skills
Design Technology nurtures a unique blend of technical and transferable skills. Students graduate with fluency in design thinking, communication, and innovation — ready for careers in engineering, architecture, product development, UX/UI design, or entrepreneurship. For those pursuing creative industries, DT is a launchpad for making meaningful impact through thoughtful design.

Design Technology at St Lawrence College blends innovation, functionality and imagination — equipping students to think, prototype and problem-solve like true creatives in an ever-evolving world.
Innovation in Action
More than just making, DT at SLC is about meaningful creation. Students explore the full lifecycle of design: from concept and planning to execution and evaluation. They work across a wide range of materials and technologies, gaining hands-on experience with 3D printing, laser cutting, electronics, and textiles. From product design to wearable tech, every brief encourages purpose-driven innovation.
Personal Projects, Real Outcomes
With a curriculum that evolves from Key Stage 3 through to A-Level, students take on increasingly ambitious and personalised design challenges. At GCSE and A-Level, projects are student-led, allowing for exploration in areas like sustainability, inclusive design, smart materials, and engineered systems. Whether designing for user needs or tackling environmental issues, our students are empowered to think critically and creatively.
Please see our academics page for more details.
A Studio for Discovery
Our well-equipped workshops are dynamic spaces where creativity meets precision. Students use professional-standard CAD software and fabrication tools to realise their ideas, guided by expert tuition and individual feedback. This environment fosters independent thinking and problem-solving skills — essential not just for exams, but for future pathways.
Design Thinking Beyond the Classroom
DT students regularly engage in national competitions like Design Ventura and experience workshops led by real-world designers and engineers. The department also offers exciting enrichment such as Robot Wars, DT Ambassadors, and trips to the Design Museum and V&A — extending learning beyond textbooks and into authentic, inspiring contexts.
Future-Ready Skills
Design Technology nurtures a unique blend of technical and transferable skills. Students graduate with fluency in design thinking, communication, and innovation — ready for careers in engineering, architecture, product development, UX/UI design, or entrepreneurship. For those pursuing creative industries, DT is a launchpad for making meaningful impact through thoughtful design.

At St Lawrence College we offer a supportive, caring and challenging environment, founded on traditional Christian values, where children are given every opportunity to fulfil their potential.
Sixth Form
St Lawrence College aims for educational excellence, and nearly all of the Upper Sixth will continue to Higher Education at University.
The pastoral care in the school is very good indeed. There is a house based system, so that every child has a Housemaster or Housemistress who is the key point of contact both for them and for their parents, and each child also has a personal tutor who is responsible for helping to oversee their academic and general development. Besides meeting with their tutee every week, the tutor will show an interest in their various activities and contributions around the school and support them at school events.
Being both a boarding and a day school is a great strength in terms of the opportunities this gives for integration between pupils from different backgrounds and different parts of the world. Boarders and day pupils are easily able to forge friendships which allow for cultural exchange. For local day pupils, being able to meet and mix with pupils from all over the world is a great opportunity to broaden horizons, and this international mix is really good for boarders as well.
We place a strong emphasis on mental wellbeing and how this links to academic success and indeed to success in all areas of school life. Assemblies, displays around the school, and visits from outside speakers help to promote awareness of these important matters. We also use a pastoral tool called Affective Social Tracking – or AS Tracking – in which pupils complete twice yearly assessments which reveal how they are self-regulating and how they are thinking and seeing the world around them. This helps to guide the staff in their pastoral interactions with pupils. Our pupils have a range of people to whom they can turn to discuss any problems or worries they may have: senior pupils and prefects; tutors; housemasters or housemistresses; medical staff; careers adviser; universities adviser; the Chaplain; school counsellors.
All of these things are underpinned by a strong Christian ethos which is at the heart of the school. This isn’t just about regular Chapel services, although these do form a really important part of each week, but about how pupils live their lives, how they treat each other, how they interact with one another and all those around them. This is a school where pupils can be themselves and are respected and celebrated for who they are, and this is the key to why it is such a happy and supportive community.

Sixth Form
St Lawrence College aims for educational excellence, and nearly all of the Upper Sixth will continue to Higher Education at University.
Academic
We are ambitious for every child and are proud of our academic record. We recognise that education, in its truest sense, is measured not just in results but by preparing young people for a successful future. The learning programme is based on the National Curriculum but always aims to go beyond those confines and to make the process accessible, relevant, meaningful, stimulating and enjoyable for all pupils. Learning across the curriculum is underpinned by an emphasis on creative problem-solving which teaches children how to learn and develops a real sense of intellectual enquiry.
Personal attention is given within small classes where talents are recognised and needs are catered for. Teaching is carefully differentiated to stretch and inspire the most able and to support and encourage those whose confidence is still developing. Specialist teaching from an early stage ensures that teachers’ passion for, and knowledge of, their subjects rubs off on their pupils. Every lesson is characterised by a sense of teachers and pupils working closely together to share mutual interests and achieve common goals.
In Years 3-6, whilst the core subjects of English, Maths and Science take priority, the curriculum continues to broaden with focussed Art, Design, Science, Geography, History, Religious Studies, Music, PSHE, Computing and Teaching and Learning skills.
Pupils benefit from access to exceptional facilities and resources including a sand based and water based hockey pitch, large sports hall and Theatre. Regular Enrichment Days, field trips and visits encourage them to think for themselves, to take increasing responsibility for their own learning, and to understand their social, moral and environmental obligations.
As well as achieving results in the Kent Test which are well above KCC expectations, Junior School pupils have a proud record of success at gaining Senior School scholarships. And for those who may be looking towards Grammar Schools, focused preparation for the 11+ Kent Test is a key priority.
Ultimately, the school is well aware that every child must be equipped with a raft of skills to thrive in an extremely competitive world, and to make the most of a future which will doubtless hold many challenges and surprises.
11+ Kent Test/Senior Scholarships
Although many of our children move through to the Senior school of St Lawrence, we also support children to join local Grammar or High schools.
In the Prep School the timetable includes an hour a week of Thinking and Learning Skills (TLS). In Years 4 and 5, TLS lessons concentrate to a greater extent on the Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning skills that candidates need in readiness for the Kent Test.
The Maths scheme of work in Year 5 is carefully tailored to accelerate coverage of all the necessary groundwork, and to emphasise the problem-solving element of the Kent Test syllabus. Over half of our children are working a year in advance of national expectations and 30% achieved the highest possible age on their respective tests. Also in Year 5, an additional hour of focused preparation is provided each week via the Saturday morning Activities programme complemented with a summer holiday revision camp.

How to Apply for Senior School Admissions:
Welcome to St Lawrence College Senior School Admissions! If you’re considering St Lawrence College for your child, we invite you to visit us in person. During your visit, we’ll give you a tour of our campus and introduce you to a member of our Senior Leadership Team, who will be happy to answer any questions you may have. This is the perfect opportunity to see our school in action and learn more about how we nurture academic success and personal growth in a supportive environment.
If your family is international and interested in St Lawrence College, we ensure the admissions process is smooth and welcoming from start to finish. Our Admissions Team would be happy to arrange a virtual call for you. During this call, we can guide you through our fantastic immersive 360 tour of the school, giving you a detailed look at our facilities and everything we have to offer. You’ll also have the chance to meet some of our key staff members, so you can get a real feel for the vibrant and supportive community here at St Lawrence College.
Senior Admissions Process
Step 1: Visit the School
We warmly invite you to visit us in person! During your visit, you’ll enjoy a guided tour of our wonderful school, meet our dedicated staff and enthusiastic pupils, and have the chance to sit down with a member of our Senior Leadership Team.
We offer individual school tours during term time and during holiday periods, as well as taster visits for prospective pupils. We are also delighted to offer remote visits for families who are unable to visit us in person.
If you wish to book either an Open Day or an individual visit, please click here. Alternatively, do not hesitate to contact the Admissions Team on admissions@slcuk.com or +44 (0)1843 808080.
Step 2: Admissions Process
If you feel that St Lawrence College is the right place for your child, families are able to complete an online admissions process using our Admissions Portal, or alternatively a Registration Form, PDF version, found within the Registration Pack.
Step 3: Registration Fee
A non-refundable registration fee of £120 is required when submitting the form.
Step 4: Required Documents
Please include a copy of your child’s most recent school report and their passport along with the Registration Form.
Step 5: Interview and Assessments
Your child will then have a friendly interview and complete two assessment papers in Maths and English—or in EAL if English isn’t their first language. These assessments are not a pass or fail test; rather, they help us gain a deeper understanding of your child’s current academic levels and how they might fit within their year group. If anything stands out, we’ll discuss it with you at this stage.
Following this, our Admissions Team will reach out to your child’s current school for a School Reference or, if applicable, a Suitability for Boarding Reference.
Step 6: Optional Taster Day
We also offer a taster day, where your child can spend time with us, experiencing life at St Lawrence College firsthand. It’s a wonderful way for everyone to get to know each other and to explore all that our school has to offer.
Step 7: Offers and Acceptance
After reviewing the admissions process, offers are made under the guidance of the Head of College. To secure your child’s place, simply return the Acceptance Form and pay the deposit, completing the final step of the entry process.
This step-by-step process ensures that both your family and our school feel confident and excited about the journey ahead at St Lawrence College.

Students are encouraged to contact the Mrs Semlyen, our Head of Careers directly to book a 1 to1 appointment. A visit to careers library can be worthwhile and students will find a range of prospectuses for university along with other guides. But to explore your own career the following websites are recommended:
UCAS stands for Universities and Colleges Admissions Service. It’s the centralised service that students use to apply to university. More information here.
A good all round website that covers lots of aspects of careers. More information here.
A brilliant website – great for answering the question “What can I do with a degree in …?”, but really good for all things careers. More information here.
The website for the Russell Group universities – some great resources if you want to know more about this group of universities and what they are looking for. More information here.
Link your account to the school, and you can personalise how this website can help you. More information here.
If you are intending on applying for medical or dental school this website, along with our MDV specialist preparation, is the go-to website for you. More information here.
If you intend to apply to the US for college/university, use this website to help you select the colleges that best suit you. Join our specialist US Preparation Pathway to increase your chances of success. More information here.
This website allows you to watch short video clips of people in a wide range of job sectors. More information here.
An amazing website to build your life skills: financial, career, professional, and personal – you can complete modules and track your progress. More information here.
It does what it says in its name – help you to find the path you could take into your chosen career. More information here.
NATIONAL CAREERS SERVICE
The National Careers Service is a service provided by the Government. You can secure an independent and impartial careers guidance meeting via this service. More information here.
Also, explore our section on labour market information, which helps you to understand which job sectors are growing, or shrinking which will you plan your successful career.
